LOGOS is the analytical brain of the AIMarket federation. It queries every component — oracles, scanners, treasuries, reputation graphs, bridges — through transparent `hub.invoke()` proxy and answers natural-language questions: > "How long will the Treasury last?" "Which hub has the most critical findings?" "Why was Hub B slow yesterday?" "Show me the reputation leaderboard." ## Architecture graph TB subgraph "LOGOS Node" FE[🧠 LOGOS Frontend

Build with `docker build -f Dockerfile.standalone -t logos .` from the repo root. ### Frontend cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev # → http://localhost:5199 ## Federation Tier Deploy # Monorepo: included in the full fleet ./start.sh --everything # Standalone: docker build -f Dockerfile.standalone -t logos . docker run -p 5199:5199 -e LOGOS_HUB_URL=https://modelmarket.dev logos Container | Purpose --- | --- `logos` | Analytics engine (FastAPI + React + Nginx) `logos-postgres` | Analytics store (Postgres 16, or SQLite for dev) `hub` | Federation routing + invoke proxy `monitor` | Alien Monitor 3D ecosystem graph 4 containers. Visit AICOM (AIMarket) → Hlido Editor · 2026-08-05 AICOM proposes a full open economy for autonomous agents: a 13-agent factory that takes a brief through spec, code, QA, security and deploy; a federated hub where shipped capabilities and oracles are signed, indexed and invokable; and pay-per-call settlement over micropayment channels, all self-hosted under MIT/Apache-2.0 with an explicit "no hosted black box — your keys, your data, your host" stance. Seventeen oracles are listed with real mathematical substance (verifiable randomness, optimal transport, persistent homology, graph spectra, Gaussian-process uncertainty), each with Ed25519-signed receipts and optional post-quantum ML-DSA, alongside 377 passing tests. The single most credible thing on the page is the smallest: the Chronos × Platon beacon is labelled "research/prototype crypto honesty", with post-quantum signing off by default. A project that flags its own cryptography as prototype rather than marketing it as quantum-safe is telling you something true, and it is the reason this scores as high as it does. Everything else argues for caution. The scope — factory, marketplace, protocol, oracles, 3D visualisers, Telegram and Discord bots, YouTube release broadcasting, fleet observability — is enormous for what appears to be a very small team, and breadth at that ratio usually means shallow depth somewhere. It is hosted on GitHub Pages, has no adoption evidence, named users, or third-party audit, and "377 tests green" measures self-authored tests, not correctness. Reviewed from the public surface only. ## Why FADING FADING (60) — real technical substance (17 mathematically specified oracles, Ed25519-signed receipts, permissive licensing, genuine self-hosting) and notable intellectual honesty in labelling its own beacon cryptography as research/prototype with post-quantum signing off by default. Held at FADING because the scope is enormous relative to apparent team size, there is no adoption evidence, no third-party audit, and self-authored passing tests are not independent validation of a system that signs and settles value. ## What it does well * Labels its own Chronos × Platon beacon as research/prototype cryptography rather than marketing it as production-grade * Post-quantum ML-DSA available but off by default — a conservative, correct default * 17 oracles with genuine mathematical specificity, each shipping Ed25519-signed receipts * Fully self-hosted and permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0) — no hosted black box, forkable in every part * Coherent compounding loop: factory ships a capability, hub indexes it, next run discovers and reuses it * Verify step is built into the invocation flow — discover, invoke, verify the signed proof, settle ## What it fails at * Scope (factory, marketplace, protocol, oracles, 3D visualisers, bots, broadcasting, observability) is enormous relative to apparent team size * No adoption evidence, named users, or production deployments on the public surface * '377 tests green' counts self-authored tests — not independent validation of a value-signing system * No third-party security audit despite cryptographic signing and on-chain settlement being central * Hosted on GitHub Pages with no institutional footprint or stated continuity commitment * Heavy mythological branding (Dioscuri, Helios, Metis, Gaia, Skopos, Chronos, Platon) obscures rather than explains what each component does ## Red flags * [object Object] ## Best for * Researchers and builders exploring self-hosted, non-custodial agent-to-agent economies * Anyone who needs verifiable-math oracles with signed proofs and is able to audit the code themselves * Teams that require full self-hosting and permissive licensing over managed convenience ## Not recommended for * Production systems settling real value — the project labels key cryptography as prototype * Buyers needing an independent security audit before trusting signed receipts * Chronos × Platon beacon labelled research/prototype cryptography by the project itself — source (2026-08-05) verified * 377 tests green — source (2026-08-05) * Adoption, production deployments, or third-party security audit — source (2026-08-05) ##
